title: Connecting entanglement growth with local integrals of motion in the disordered Fermi-Hubbard model
authors: Ahad Nokhostin Helm, Brandon Leipner-Johns, Rachel Wortis
abstract: Generically a quantum system initialized in an unentangled state will, under unitary dynamics, rapidly become entangled, a process closely related to information transport and to thermalization. Disorder can suppress the growth of entanglement and result in memory of initial conditions. In non-interacting systems this arises from localization of single-particle states, the occupancy of which is fixed by the initial condition. In interacting systems similar localized conserved quantities persist, but with the added feature that they are coupled, resulting in entanglement growth which is distinct from both non-interacting localized systems and from generic ergodic systems. The Fermi-Hubbard model has two degrees of freedom per site -- charge and spin -- and disorder may be present in both of these. We study the growth of entanglement in two scenarios -- disorder in charge equal and unequal to that in spin, and determine the distinct contributions of charge and spin degrees of freedom by expanding the Hamiltonian in terms of a set of optimally localized conserved quantities with separate charge and spin character. We find that coupling between charge and spin is significantly weaker than charge-charge and spin-spin coupling. While this decoupling is present in all our results, it is only apparent when the strength of the disorder in the two sectors is different such that there is a separation between the characteristic timescales of the contributions to entanglement made by charge and by spin.
summary: This paper analyzes entanglement growth in the disordered Fermi-Hubbard model by expanding the Hamiltonian using Local Integrals of Motion (LIOMs). The key finding is that when charge and spin disorder are unequal, the system exhibits sequential entanglement buildup dominated first by charge dynamics and later by spin dynamics. This method offers a detailed theoretical pathway to disentangle coupled many-body physics into contributions from distinct physical degrees of freedom.
main_problem: The study investigates how disorder affects entanglement growth dynamics in interacting quantum systems, specifically by connecting this growth to local integrals of motion (LIOMs). The goal is to understand the distinct contributions of charge and spin degrees of freedom.
main_result: The analysis reveals that while coupling between charge and spin is generally weaker than intra-species couplings, this decoupling becomes clearly apparent when disorder strengths in the two sectors are unequal. For unequal disorder, entanglement growth exhibits distinct early-time phases dominated sequentially by charge and then spin dynamics.
method: The authors employ an advanced theoretical technique involving expanding the Hamiltonian in terms of optimally localized conserved quantities (LIOMs) with separate charge and spin characters. Entanglement entropy is calculated using these LIOM expansions and comparing results from various truncation orders.
model_or_system: The system studied is the disordered Fermi-Hubbard model, which possesses two degrees of freedom per site: charge and spin. The Hamiltonian includes hopping, on-site repulsion ($U$), and disorder potentials applied independently to the charge ($\epsilon_i$) and spin ($h_i$) sectors.
key_observables: Bipartite von Neumann entanglement entropy $S(t)$, which is tracked as a function of time (or $\log(t)$).
important_parameters: Disorder strengths in charge ($	ext{W}_{	ext{ch}}$) and spin ($	ext{W}_{	ext{sp}}$), interaction strength ($U$), and system size ($L$). The comparison between equal vs. unequal disorder regimes is crucial.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the successful expansion of the full Hamiltonian into a basis of LIOMs, allowing for systematic truncation at different orders (e.g., $	ext{H}_{	ext{liom}1}$, $	ext{H}_{	ext{liom}2}$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate entanglement entropy growth curves comparing exact results against various LIOM truncations; they also show the spatial decay of coupling coefficients and compare dynamics under equal versus unequal disorder conditions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the model, develops the mathematical framework using LIOMs to decompose the Hamiltonian, calculates entanglement entropy for different disorder regimes (equal vs. unequal), and compares the results obtained from various orders of approximation in the LIOM expansion.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool—the LIOM expansion—to dissect complex many-body dynamics into contributions from specific conserved quantities. The ability to separate charge and spin dynamics based on disorder asymmetry is highly relevant for understanding correlated materials where different degrees of freedom might localize or evolve on distinct timescales.

For U = 0, the entanglement has a rapid ini- tial rise to a peak at a time of order one, followed by a dip and then saturation. This behaviour is consistent with results in single-component systems. The reason for this structure can be understood by considering a single particle initially placed at one site. Without in- teractions, up and down spins are independent and An- derson localized.
